# Shader library reference

<!-- Generated by `jasperengine-editor shaders --library all --doc docs/shaders/library.md`
from the manifests of engine/shaderlib/library/*.frag. Do not edit by hand: change the
manifests (or editor/shader/ShaderLibraryDoc.cpp) and regenerate. -->

The engine ships ready-made shaders, referenced as `library:<name>`. Pick one in the
material's **Shader** row (mesh shaders, per submesh) or in the component's custom shader
(UI, Points, Sky); from Lua set `material.shader = "library:toon"` (and
`material:setShaderParam`, `setShaderTexture`, `setShaderFeature`), from MCP `list_shaders`
describes them. Unset parameters and textures take the defaults listed here.

`ui` shaders are for the component UI (Image, Text, Polygon). HTML/CSS UI documents (UI
Document component) draw with their own shaders; their GPU effects are a library of their own,
`effect(<name>, ...)` in CSS (shader type `UI_EFFECT`, ids `@effects/<name>`, a project's own
`.frag` declared with `@effect`): `jasper://docs/html-ui-effects`, MCP `list_ui_effects`.

## Lighting modes

A mesh shader lists the lighting modes it supports; the first is its default (Auto). The
material's **Lighting** row picks one of them:

| Mode | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| Per pixel (`pixel`) | Every light of the object is evaluated per pixel: diffuse, specular, shadows, spot masks. | Close-up, important objects; the most expensive. |
| Per vertex (`vertex`) | Every light is evaluated per vertex and interpolated: diffuse only (no specular, shadows or spot mask; a spot's cone still applies). | Mobile, background and dense scenery, many lights; the cheapest lit mode. Coarse on large triangles near point lights. |
| Mixed (`mixed`) | Each light follows its own **Shading** (Light inspector, Lua `light.shading`): Per pixel, Per vertex, or Both (per pixel here). | A main light per pixel with shadows and fill lights per vertex. |
| None (`none`) | Unlit. | Effects, stylised art, UI-like 3D. |

A lit mode in a scene without lights (or with the mesh's Receive Lights off) draws the
shader's unlit colour. Shadows come only from per-pixel lights that cast them.

**Lights per object.** A scene may have any number of lights. For each mesh (an instanced
batch counts as one, by its bounds) the engine picks the lights that reach it: every
directional light, and the point and spot lights whose range reaches its bounds (a spot
also by its cone), ranked by their contribution. The first **Max Lights Per Object** (scene
setting, 1 to 16, default 8; Lua `scene.maxLightsPerObject`) are evaluated as above; the
others are folded into the object's ambient (spherical harmonics), so lights never pop. The
setting picks a compile tier of 4, 8 or 16 lights: fewer is cheaper on every lit shader.
A script that changes it at runtime makes an export include the variants of every tier.

## Blend modes

The material's **Blend Mode** (UI, Points and Lines components: their own Blend Mode) is
Auto by default: the shader's default state (`blend` below), else the engine's legacy alpha
blend. The engine compiles each variant for the blend it draws with (`BLEND_*`), so a shader
needs no setting of its own for it:

| Blend | Factors | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Opaque | none | Solid surfaces; draws in the opaque queue and writes depth. |
| Alpha | src alpha, 1 - src alpha | Glass, fades, soft sprites. |
| Premultiplied | 1, 1 - src alpha | Textures whose colour is already multiplied by their alpha (no dark fringes when filtered). A shader that samples a texture takes it as premultiplied; Sprite reads its texture as premultiplied; shaders that compute their alpha (Particle, Hologram, Rim, Water) premultiply it themselves. |
| Additive | src alpha, 1 | Glows, fire, lasers: adds light; the fog fades it out. |
| Multiply | dst colour, 0 | Dirt, fake shadows: darkens what is behind; transparent parts (alpha 0) leave it unchanged. |

Anything but Opaque draws in the transparent queue, sorted by **Sort Priority** (lower
first), then far to near; Depth Write Auto is off for it. A shader's state may change with
its features or keywords (`@state[...]` rules below): Hologram's Default blend Alpha makes it
alpha blended, Decal's Multiply makes it multiply. A material value always wins.

## Reading an entry

- **Lighting**: the supported modes, the default first.
- **Inputs**: the vertex data the shader reads (`position`, `normals`, `tangents`, `uv1`,
  `uv2`, `color` = vertex colour times instance colour, `rawcolor` = the vertex colour
  alone, `smoothnormals` = the normal averaged over the vertices sharing a position, made by
  the engine); "with X" inputs only while feature X is on ("without X": while off). A mesh
  that lacks one still draws (normal +Y, UV 0, white). `scenedepth` and `scenecolor` are
  the scene inputs (`includes/scene.glsl`), listed again under **Reads the scene**.
- **Reads the scene**: the shader samples the opaque scene's depth or a copy of its colour.
  The engine makes them only in camera passes that draw such a shader: a depth pre-pass
  (shared with SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass when one runs) and one copy of the
  opaque scene and sky (Scene Color Scale: half resolution by default). Extra GPU work on
  mobile; the shader draws in the transparent queue and does not see other transparent
  objects.
- **Default state**: what Auto resolves to; `shadows off` means the object casts no shadow
  even when its mesh casts shadows; `priority -1` is added to the material's Sort Priority
  (it draws before what has the same Sort Priority in its queue). "With X" lines apply while
  feature or keyword value X is on.
- **Depth program**: the shader moves vertices or discards fragments, and its shadows and
  depth pre-pass do the same.
- **Properties**: colours are given in sRGB as edited (stored linear); "with X" rows show
  only while feature X is on. **Features** are compile-time switches (no cost when off);
  **keywords** pick one value of a group (the first is the default; the define is
  `<GROUP>_<VALUE>`).

## Basic

<a id="libraryunlit"></a>
### Unlit (`library:unlit`)

Base colour times base map, optionally times vertex colour, without lighting; optional alpha clip, whose shadows are cut out too. Soft intersections and a camera near fade for particles on meshes (instanced quads of a particle system): either one makes it alpha blended without depth writes or shadows. Soft reads the scene depth: on mobile that is an extra depth pass of the opaque meshes in every camera that sees it (none when SSAO or SSR already made one).

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Basic.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`; `scenedepth` with `SOFT`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend opaque; with `SOFT`: blend alpha, depth write off, shadows off; with `NEAR_FADE`: blend alpha, depth write off, shadows off.
- **Depth program**: yes (shadows and depth follow its vertices and clipping).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Base colour |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `alphaCutoff` | range 0 to 1 | 0.5 | Alpha cutoff (with `ALPHA_CLIP`) |
| `softness` | float | 0.5 | Softness (world units) (with `SOFT`) |
| `nearFadeStart` | float | 0.3 | Near fade: invisible at (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |
| `nearFadeEnd` | float | 1.5 | Near fade: whole from (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticContrast` | range 0 to 1 | 0.45 | Contrast (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticRotation` | range 0 to 1 | 0 | Rotation (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white; built-in particle with `PARTICLE_TEXTURE` | Base map |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VERTEX_COLOR` | off | Vertex colour |
| `ALPHA_CLIP` | off | Alpha clip |
| `SOFT` | off | Soft intersections (fade where it meets geometry; reads the scene depth) |
| `NEAR_FADE` | off | Camera near fade |
| `STOCHASTIC` | off | Stochastic Tiling |
| `PARTICLE_TEXTURE` | off | Built-in soft particle texture (when no base map is set) |

## Lit

<a id="librarysimple_lit"></a>
### Simple Lit (`library:simple_lit`)

Blinn-Phong lighting: diffuse from every light, specular and shadows from the pixel lights, optional normal map and emission. The mobile tier of Lit.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Lit.
- **Lighting**: per pixel (default), per vertex, mixed.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Base colour |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `specularColor` | colour | (0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 1) | Specular colour |
| `gloss` | range 0 to 1 | 0.5 | Glossiness |
| `normalStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Normal strength (with `NORMAL_MAP`) |
| `emissionColor` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Emission colour (with `EMISSION`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticContrast` | range 0 to 1 | 0.45 | Contrast (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticRotation` | range 0 to 1 | 0 | Rotation (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map |
| `u_normalTexture` | flat normal | Normal map (with `NORMAL_MAP`) |
| `u_emissionTexture` | white | Emission map (with `EMISSION`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VERTEX_COLOR` | off | Vertex colour |
| `NORMAL_MAP` | off | Normal map |
| `EMISSION` | off | Emission |
| `STOCHASTIC` | off | Stochastic Tiling |

<a id="libraryvertex_lit"></a>
### Vertex Lit (`library:vertex_lit`)

Base colour times base map, lit per vertex: the ambient plus the diffuse of the object's lights. The cheapest lit shader.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Lit.
- **Lighting**: per vertex (default).
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Base colour |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `emissionColor` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Emission colour (with `EMISSION`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticContrast` | range 0 to 1 | 0.45 | Contrast (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticRotation` | range 0 to 1 | 0 | Rotation (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map |
| `u_emissionTexture` | white | Emission map (with `EMISSION`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VERTEX_COLOR` | off | Vertex colour |
| `EMISSION` | off | Emission |
| `STOCHASTIC` | off | Stochastic Tiling |

## Stylized

<a id="librarydirectional_tint"></a>
### Directional Tint (`library:directional_tint`)

Kenney's directional tint: one colour per world axis, blended by the world normal, times the base map. Unlit. White in all three colours is neutral, Kenney's original defaults; the defaults here are a sample tint (warm tops, purple and red sides).

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Stylized.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `normals`, `uv1`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Colour (multiplies all three) |
| `colorA` | colour | (1, 0.78, 0.25, 1) | Colour A (faces along Y: top, bottom) |
| `colorB` | colour | (0.56, 0.33, 0.86, 1) | Colour B (faces along X) |
| `colorC` | colour | (0.92, 0.26, 0.3, 1) | Colour C (faces along Z) |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map |

<a id="libraryfake_lit"></a>
### Fake Lit (`library:fake_lit`)

Lighting faked without lights: surfaces facing down and away from the camera blend to a shadow colour, with optional matcap shine, baked shadow texture, vertex AO, emission and axis fog. Cheap; no scene lights needed.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Stylized.
- **Lighting**: none (default), per vertex.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals`, `uv1`, `color`; `uv2` with `SHADOW_TEXTURE`; `rawcolor` with `VERTEX_AO`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `shadowColor` | colour | (0.36, 0.33, 0.52, 1) | Shadow colour |
| `shadowPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 1.5 | Downward shadow power |
| `shadowStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 0.6 | Downward shadow strength |
| `rimScale` | range 0 to 2 | 0.5 | Edge shadow scale |
| `rimPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 2.5 | Edge shadow power |
| `matcapGain` | range 0 to 4 | 1 | Matcap gain (with `MATCAP`) |
| `matcapPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 1 | Matcap power (with `MATCAP`) |
| `shadowTextureStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Shadow texture strength (with `SHADOW_TEXTURE`) |
| `aoStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Vertex AO strength (with `VERTEX_AO`) |
| `emissionColor` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Emission colour (with `EMISSION`) |
| `fogColor` | colour | (0.62, 0.78, 0.95, 1) | Axis fog colour (with `AXIS_FOG`) |
| `fogAxis` | vector3 | (0, 0, -1) | Axis fog direction (world, unit length) (with `AXIS_FOG`) |
| `fogStart` | float | 6 | Axis fog start (from the camera) (with `AXIS_FOG`) |
| `fogLength` | float | 20 | Axis fog length (with `AXIS_FOG`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticContrast` | range 0 to 1 | 0.45 | Contrast (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticRotation` | range 0 to 1 | 0 | Rotation (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map |
| `u_matcapTexture` | black | Matcap (with `MATCAP`) |
| `u_shadowTexture` | white | Shadow texture (red, 1 = lit; UV2, else UV1) (with `SHADOW_TEXTURE`) |
| `u_emissionTexture` | white | Emission map (with `EMISSION`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCAP` | off | Matcap shine |
| `SHADOW_TEXTURE` | off | Baked shadow texture |
| `VERTEX_AO` | off | Vertex colour AO (red) |
| `EMISSION` | off | Emission |
| `AXIS_FOG` | off | Axis fog |
| `STOCHASTIC` | off | Stochastic Tiling |

<a id="librarymatcap"></a>
### Matcap (`library:matcap`)

Material capture: the colour comes from a matcap image looked up by the view-space normal, replacing, multiplying or adding to the base map. Assign a matcap image (ADD wants a shine matcap, mostly black: the default white one adds full white); unlit.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Stylized.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals`, `color`; `uv1` without `MATCAP_MODE_REPLACE`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) (without `MATCAP_MODE_REPLACE`) |
| `matcapGain` | range 0 to 4 | 1 | Matcap gain |
| `matcapPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 1 | Matcap power |
| `rimColor` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Rim colour (with `RIM`) |
| `rimPower` | range 0.5 to 16 | 4 | Rim power (with `RIM`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_matcapTexture` | white | Matcap |
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map (without `MATCAP_MODE_REPLACE`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RIM` | off | Rim light |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MATCAP_MODE` | `MATCAP_MODE_REPLACE`, `MATCAP_MODE_MULTIPLY`, `MATCAP_MODE_ADD` | Mode |

<a id="librarytoon"></a>
### Toon (`library:toon`)

Cel shading: the light falls in hard bands (or follows a ramp texture), the unlit side takes a shadow colour, with optional hard specular highlight and rim light. Receives shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Stylized.
- **Lighting**: per pixel (default), mixed, per vertex.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`; `position`, `normals` with `RIM`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Base colour |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `shadowColor` | colour | (0.42, 0.38, 0.62, 1) | Shadow colour (unlit side fill) |
| `bands` | range 1 to 8 | 2 | Bands |
| `bandSmoothness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.08 | Band edge width |
| `specularColor` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Specular colour (with `SPECULAR`) |
| `specularSize` | range 0 to 1 | 0.3 | Specular size (with `SPECULAR`) |
| `specularSmoothness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.15 | Specular edge width (with `SPECULAR`) |
| `rimColor` | HDR colour | (0.75, 0.75, 0.75, 1) | Rim colour (with `RIM`) |
| `rimPower` | range 0.5 to 16 | 4 | Rim power (with `RIM`) |
| `rimSmoothness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.1 | Rim edge width (with `RIM`) |
| `rimLitOnly` | toggle | on | Rim on the lit side only (with `RIM`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticContrast` | range 0 to 1 | 0.45 | Contrast (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticRotation` | range 0 to 1 | 0 | Rotation (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map |
| `u_rampTexture` | white | Ramp (left unlit, right lit) (with `RAMP`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RAMP` | off | Ramp texture |
| `SPECULAR` | off | Specular highlight |
| `RIM` | off | Rim light |
| `STOCHASTIC` | off | Stochastic Tiling |

<a id="librarytriplanar"></a>
### Triplanar (`library:triplanar`)

Projects a texture along the three axes and blends by the normal, so meshes need no UVs and tiling stays even. Optional separate floor and ceiling textures and a dirt overlay. Unlit or Lambert lit.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Stylized.
- **Lighting**: none (default), per pixel, per vertex.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `tiling` | float | 1 | Tiling (repeats per unit) |
| `sharpness` | range 1 to 16 | 4 | Blend sharpness |
| `noiseTiling` | float | 0.15 | Dirt noise tiling (repeats per unit) (with `NOISE_MASK`) |
| `dirtColor` | colour | (0.23, 0.17, 0.11, 1) | Dirt colour (with `NOISE_MASK`) |
| `dirtStrength` | range 0 to 1 | 0.65 | Dirt strength (with `NOISE_MASK`) |
| `dirtContrast` | range 0.5 to 8 | 2.5 | Dirt contrast (with `NOISE_MASK`) |
| `stochasticCellSize` | range 0.25 to 4 | 1 | Cell Size (with `STOCHASTIC`) |
| `stochasticBlendSharpness` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Blend Sharpness (with `STOCHASTIC`) |

<a id="libraryvertex_color"></a>

The mesh's vertex colours times a tint, optionally times a texture. Unlit, or Lambert lit per vertex or per pixel.

| `TEXTURE` | off | Texture |

## Effects

<a id="librarydecal"></a>
### Decal (`library:decal`)

Mesh decal: texture times tint on a quad laid on a surface, alpha blended, pulled towards the camera by a depth offset so it does not z-fight; no shadows. Default blend Multiply darkens what is under it instead (dirt, fake shadows).

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, depth write off, depth offset -1, -1, shadows off; with `DECAL_BLEND_MULTIPLY`: blend multiply.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `opacity` | range 0 to 1 | 1 | Opacity |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Decal |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VERTEX_COLOR` | off | Vertex colour |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DECAL_BLEND` | `DECAL_BLEND_ALPHA`, `DECAL_BLEND_MULTIPLY` | Default blend |

<a id="librarydepth_fade"></a>
### Depth fade (`library:depth_fade`)

Fog cards, light shafts and soft volumes: texture times tint and vertex colour, fading where it meets geometry (no hard line where a card crosses the ground or a wall), close to the camera and far away, optionally scrolling, masked and faded when seen edge-on. Alpha blended (the Additive default blend for light shafts), both faces, no depth write or shadows. The soft intersections read the scene depth: on mobile that is an extra depth pass of the opaque meshes in every camera that sees it (none when SSAO or SSR already made one); turn Soft off for camera fades alone.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`; `scenedepth` with `SOFT`; `position`, `normals` with `EDGE_FADE`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, cull off (both faces), depth write off, shadows off; with `FADE_BLEND_ADDITIVE`: blend additive.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | HDR colour | (1, 1, 1, 0.6) | Tint |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `softness` | float | 1 | Softness (world units) (with `SOFT`) |
| `nearFadeStart` | float | 0.5 | Near fade: invisible at (world units from the camera) |
| `nearFadeEnd` | float | 3 | Near fade: whole from (world units from the camera) |
| `farFadeStart` | float | 60 | Far fade: starts at (world units from the camera) |
| `farFadeEnd` | float | 80 | Far fade: invisible from (world units from the camera) |
| `scrollSpeed` | vector2 | (0.03, 0.01) | Scroll (UV per second) (with `SCROLL`) |
| `edgeFadePower` | range 0.25 to 8 | 1.5 | Edge-on fade power (with `EDGE_FADE`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Base map (fog, beam) |
| `u_maskTexture` | white | Shape mask (red times alpha, not tiled or scrolled) (with `MASK`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SOFT` | on | Soft intersections (reads the scene depth) |
| `SCROLL` | off | Scrolling base map |
| `MASK` | off | Shape mask |
| `EDGE_FADE` | off | Fade when seen edge-on |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FADE_BLEND` | `FADE_BLEND_ALPHA`, `FADE_BLEND_ADDITIVE` | Default blend |

<a id="librarydissolve"></a>

Burns the surface away where a noise texture is below the cutoff, with a glowing edge band; both faces drawn, so the inside shows through the holes. Shadows get the same holes.

- **Lighting**: none (default), per pixel.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`; `normals` with `WORLD_NOISE`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, cull off (both faces).
- **Depth program**: yes (shadows and depth follow its vertices and clipping).

| `edgeWidth` | range 0 to 0.5 | 0.08 | Edge width (noise units) |
| `edgeColor` | HDR colour | (2.5, 1.2, 0.35, 1) | Edge colour |

| Feature | Default | Description |

| `VERTEX_COLOR` | off | Vertex colour |

Sprite-sheet animation on a mesh: plays the frames of a columns x rows sheet at a frame rate, looping or holding the last frame, optionally crossfading between frames. Alpha blended by default; alpha clip for opaque cutouts, which also cast shadows of the frame's shape.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend alpha; without `ALPHA_CLIP`: shadows off.
- **Depth program**: yes (shadows and depth follow its vertices and clipping).

<a id="libraryglass"></a>
### Glass (`library:glass`)

Glass and clear plastic: the scene behind it bent by its normals (index of refraction and thickness, optional normal map), tinted and absorbed along the path through it, a fresnel reflection of the scene's environment (the reflection probe around it, else the sky's environment map, else the reflection colour; REFLECTION_MAP gives it a cubemap of its own instead), a glint of the per-pixel lights; BLUR frosts it. Reads the scene colour and depth: on mobile a copy of the screen (half resolution by default), a split of the render pass and an extra depth-only pass of the opaque meshes (none when SSAO or SSR already made one). Alpha blended (transparent queue), no depth write, casts no shadows. Transparent objects behind the glass are not seen through it (it shows the scene colour, which holds only opaque objects and the sky): keep them in front of it or make them opaque.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none (default), per pixel.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals`, `scenedepth`, `scenecolor`; `uv1` with `NORMAL_MAP`; `environment` without `REFLECTION_MAP`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one) and the scene colour (a copy of the opaque scene, at the scene's Scene Color Scale), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, depth write off, shadows off.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | colour | (0.92, 0.97, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `ior` | range 1 to 2.5 | 1.45 | Index of refraction |
| `thickness` | float | 0.25 | Thickness (world units the view travels inside) |
| `absorptionColor` | colour | (0.45, 0.8, 0.75, 1) | Absorption colour (thick glass turns to it) |
| `absorption` | float | 0 | Absorption (per world unit of path) |
| `reflectionColor` | colour | (0.8, 0.86, 0.95, 1) | Reflection colour (times the environment or the cubemap; alone without either) |
| `reflectionStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Reflection strength |
| `specularColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Specular colour (per pixel lights) |
| `gloss` | range 0 to 1 | 0.9 | Glossiness (per pixel lights) |
| `normalStrength` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Normal strength (with `NORMAL_MAP`) |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Normal map tiling (xy) and offset (zw) (with `NORMAL_MAP`) |
| `blurRadius` | range 0 to 4 | 1.5 | Blur radius (texels of the scene colour copy) (with `BLUR`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_normalTexture` | flat normal | Normal map (with `NORMAL_MAP`) |
| `u_reflectionTexture` | black | Reflection cubemap (cube map) (with `REFLECTION_MAP`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NORMAL_MAP` | off | Normal map |
| `REFLECTION_MAP` | off | Reflection cubemap (instead of the environment) |
| `BLUR` | off | Frosted (blurred) |

<a id="libraryheat_haze"></a>
### Heat Haze (`library:heat_haze`)

Shimmer over fire, exhausts and portals: the scene behind the mesh wobbled by two layers of a scrolling noise texture, as strong as the mask texture, the vertex and instance alpha and the soft edge (UV border for quads and sprites, fresnel for volumes) allow. Reads the scene colour: on mobile a copy of the screen (half resolution by default) and a split of the render pass; SOFT also reads the scene depth (an extra depth-only pass of the opaque meshes, none when SSAO or SSR already made one). Without SOFT, a shift that lands on an object in front of the haze pulls that object's colour into it (a smear along its outline): turn SOFT on where objects pass in front. Transparent objects behind the haze are hidden where it is at full strength (it shows the scene colour, which holds only opaque objects and the sky), faintly seen where it fades. The UV soft edge assumes 0..1 UVs (an atlas sprite fades at its rect's place in the atlas; use FRESNEL or NONE there). Alpha blended, no depth write, both faces (give a closed volume cull back), casts no shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`, `scenecolor`; `position`, `normals` with `EDGE_FADE_FRESNEL`; `scenedepth` with `SOFT`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one) and the scene colour (a copy of the opaque scene, at the scene's Scene Color Scale), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, cull off (both faces), depth write off, shadows off.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `strength` | range 0 to 0.1 | 0.012 | Distortion (screen UV) |
| `noiseTiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Noise tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `scrollSpeed` | vector2 | (0, -0.6) | Noise scroll (UV per second) |
| `secondScrollSpeed` | vector2 | (0.07, -0.9) | Second noise layer scroll (UV per second, 1.7 times smaller) |
| `tint` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `edgeWidth` | range 0.01 to 0.5 | 0.25 | Soft edge width (UV) (with `EDGE_FADE_UV`) |
| `fresnelPower` | range 0.25 to 8 | 1.5 | Edge fade power (with `EDGE_FADE_FRESNEL`) |
| `softness` | float | 0.4 | Soft intersection (world units) (with `SOFT`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_noiseTexture` | gray | Distortion noise (red: x, green: y) |
| `u_maskTexture` | white | Mask (red times alpha) (with `MASK_TEXTURE`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MASK_TEXTURE` | off | Mask texture |
| `SOFT` | off | Soft intersection (reads the scene depth) |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `EDGE_FADE` | `EDGE_FADE_UV`, `EDGE_FADE_FRESNEL`, `EDGE_FADE_NONE` | Soft edge |

<a id="librarylattice_stretch"></a>
### Lattice Stretch (`library:lattice_stretch`)

Heat map of how much the lattices bound to the mesh squash or stretch it: white at rest, the squash colour where the volume shrinks, the stretch colour where it grows, full at range times (or 1 / range) the rest volume; folded (inside-out) cells show the squash colour. Tinted by the base map; unlit. A mesh without a lattice draws white.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.

### Line Flipbook (`library:line_flipbook`)

Animated sprite sheet along a Line or Trail Renderer: lightning, lasers, energy beams. <a id="libraryprojected_decal"></a>
### Projected decal (`library:projected_decal`)

Box projector: put it on a unit cube (1 x 1 x 1) and scale, turn and move the cube over uneven ground, stairs or a wall; the texture projects down the box's Y axis onto whatever opaque surface is inside the box, fading on steep faces (ANGLE_FADE; it may leave a pixel-wide seam along depth steps such as a stair nosing) and towards the box's top and bottom. Alpha blended (the Multiply default blend darkens instead), unlit, no shadows; works with the camera inside the box. It draws before the transparent objects of the same sort priority (its state has priority -1), so it does not paint over them. Reads the scene depth: on mobile that is an extra depth pass of the opaque meshes in every camera that sees it (none when SSAO or SSR already made one).

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Effects.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `color`, `scenedepth`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, cull front, depth write off, depth test always, shadows off, priority -1; with `DECAL_BLEND_MULTIPLY`: blend multiply.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) |
| `opacity` | range 0 to 1 | 1 | Opacity |
| `edgeFade` | range 0.001 to 0.5 | 0.1 | Fade towards the box's top and bottom (fraction of its height) |
| `angleFadeStart` | range 0 to 90 | 50 | Angle fade start (degrees from the box's up axis) (with `ANGLE_FADE`) |
| `angleFadeEnd` | range 0 to 90 | 70 | Angle fade end (degrees: gone from here) (with `ANGLE_FADE`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_baseTexture` | white | Decal |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ANGLE_FADE` | on | Fade on steep surfaces |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DECAL_BLEND` | `DECAL_BLEND_ALPHA`, `DECAL_BLEND_MULTIPLY` | Default blend |

## Nature

<a id="libraryfoliage"></a>
### Foliage (`library:foliage`)

Leaves and grass: wind sway in the vertex stage (masked by the vertex colour's red or by the height), alpha cutout, both faces drawn, light through back-lit leaves; the instance colour tints, the vertex colour does not. Shadows sway and cut out with it.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Nature.
- **Lighting**: per pixel (default), per vertex, none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`, `color`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, cull off (both faces).
- **Depth program**: yes (shadows and depth follow its vertices and clipping).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseColor` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Base colour |

<a id="librarywater"></a>
### Water (`library:water`)

Stylised water: shallow to deep colour by the view angle, two scrolling normal layers and foam anchored to the world, optional sine or Gerstner waves; lit per pixel with a specular glint, distant waves and ripples fading so they do not shimmer. Optional features: BUILTIN_TEXTURES (the engine's seamless ripples and foam noise where the material sets no texture, so no image files are needed), GERSTNER (with WAVES: four Gerstner waves, sharp crests and the surface rolling forward), REFLECTION (the sky or the reflection probe around it by Schlick's fresnel, a GGX sun glint), PLANAR_REFLECTION (with REFLECTION: the scene mirrored in the water, from a camera pass per water height at the scene's Planar Reflections resolution, else the environment), UNDERSIDE (both faces drawn: seen from below, the sky only through Snell's window, the depths mirrored around it; with library:underwater in the post-processing chain the view under the surface fades into the water), and the scene-reading DEPTH_FOAM (foam along every shore and object crossing the surface) and ABSORPTION (colour by the water's thickness; with REFRACTION the bed seen through it also loses each colour at its own rate) reading the scene depth, REFRACTION (the bed and anything under the surface bent by the ripples) the scene colour and depth, CAUSTICS (with REFRACTION: the sunlight focused on the bed). For meshes that carry their water (a spline's river or lake): FLOW (rivers: the ripples and the foam carried along the flow the vertex colour gives) and MESH_DEPTH (shore foam and shallow to deep colour from the depth the mesh's first UV set gives, with no scene-depth pass: the mobile path). Mobile cost of those: the scene depth is an extra depth-only pass of the opaque meshes (none when SSAO or SSR already made one), the scene colour a copy of the screen (half resolution by default) and a split of the render pass; REFLECTION, CAUSTICS and MESH_DEPTH are a few instructions (one cube map read for REFLECTION), GERSTNER about thirty, FLOW doubles the four texture reads; PLANAR_REFLECTION draws the scene again (at half resolution by default) for each water height a camera sees. REFRACTION needs the Alpha or Premultiplied blend (Additive and Multiply draw it unrefracted). Limits of reading the depth: no shore foam where a vertical face meets the water seen from straight above (no depth gap there), and REFRACTION leaves a faint line along outlines crossing the water (samples in front are rejected). Floats rigidbodies with a Buoyancy (Water in Lua: the surface height and normal at a point, the same waves); the waves run on the scene clock, so they hold while the game is paused. Water Excluders (boats, cabins, dry tunnels) cut it, and Water Wakes leave foam and waves on it: engine variants only scenes with those components draw. Alpha blended; casts no shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Nature.
- **Lighting**: none (default), per pixel.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals`, `waterexclusion`, `waterwake`; `scenedepth` with `DEPTH_FOAM`; `scenedepth` with `ABSORPTION`; `scenedepth`, `scenecolor` with `REFRACTION`; `environment` with `REFLECTION`; `planarreflection` with `PLANAR_REFLECTION`; `rawcolor` with `FLOW`; `uv1` with `MESH_DEPTH`.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one) and the scene colour (a copy of the opaque scene, at the scene's Scene Color Scale), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, shadows off; with `UNDERSIDE`: cull off (both faces).
- **Depth program**: yes (shadows and depth follow its vertices and clipping).

<a id="librarysprite_mask"></a>
### Sprite mask (`library:sprite_mask`)

Unity-style Sprite Mask: writes stencil 16 (bits 0xF0) in the shape of the sprite's own image (its texture rect or atlas frame; texels below the alpha cutoff write nothing), and no colour or depth. Put it on a Sprite (Sprite mask preset); sprites with the Visible inside mask preset (stencil equal 16) show only inside it, Visible outside mask (not equal) only outside. In a 3D or distance-sorted camera the mask (opaque queue) draws before the blended sprites; in a 2D camera that draws in hierarchy order, place the mask above the sprites it masks. Turn colour writes on to see it.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category 2D.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, cull off (both faces), depth write off, shadows off, colour write none, stencil always ref 16 write mask 0xf0 pass replace.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alphaCutoff` | range 0 to 1 | 0.5 | Alpha cutoff |

## Particles

<a id="libraryparticle"></a>
### Particle (`library:particle`)

Point-sprite particles: texture (sprite-sheet rect per point) times the particle colour, with alpha-as-light glow, noise erosion over the particle's life, soft intersections and a camera near fade. Draws in the Points component's blend mode (alpha by default; additive, premultiplied and multiply need no other setting); no depth write. Soft particles read the scene depth: on mobile that is an extra depth pass of the opaque meshes in every camera that sees them (none when SSAO or SSR already made one).

- **Type**: points (a Points component's custom shader); category Particles.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: depth write off.

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `glowColor` | HDR colour | (2, 1.3, 0.6, 1) | Glow colour (HDR) (with `GLOW`) |
| `glowScale` | range 0 to 4 | 1 | Glow alpha scale (with `GLOW`) |
| `glowPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 3 | Glow falloff power (with `GLOW`) |
| `erosionSoftness` | range 0.01 to 0.5 | 0.08 | Erosion edge softness (with `EROSION`) |
| `erosionTiling` | float | 1 | Erosion noise tiling (per particle) (with `EROSION`) |
| `softness` | float | 0.5 | Softness (world units) (with `SOFT`) |
| `nearFadeStart` | float | 0.3 | Near fade: invisible at (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |
| `nearFadeEnd` | float | 1.5 | Near fade: whole from (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_erosionTexture` | gray | Erosion noise (red channel) (with `EROSION`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GLOW` | off | Glow (alpha as light) |
| `EROSION` | off | Erosion (the particle's alpha dissolves it through a noise texture) |
| `SOFT` | off | Soft particles (fade where they meet geometry; reads the scene depth) |
| `NEAR_FADE` | off | Camera near fade |

<a id="libraryparticles"></a>
### Particles (`library:particles`)

The particle system shader: the particle texture (sprite-sheet frame, blended into the next with Frame Blending) times the particle colour, lit as the Renderer asks (unlit, per-vertex lit or six-way smoke lighting), plus its emission; with alpha-as-light glow, noise erosion over the particle's life, soft intersections, a camera near fade and distortion. Draws in the Renderer's blend mode; no depth write. Soft particles read the scene depth: on mobile that is an extra depth pass of the opaque meshes in every camera that sees them (none when SSAO or SSR already made one). Distortion reads the scene colour, which holds the opaque objects and the sky only (transparent objects behind a distorting particle are hidden where it is whole): on mobile a copy of the screen and a split of the render pass. Where a camera has no scene colour (a reflection probe's faces) a distorting particle draws as it would without the feature.

- **Type**: particles; category Particles.
- **Reads the scene**: the scene depth (a depth pre-pass, unless SSAO, SSR or a depth-reading post pass already runs one) and the scene colour (a copy of the opaque scene, at the scene's Scene Color Scale), in the camera passes that draw it.
- **Default state**: depth write off.

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tint` | colour | (1, 1, 1, 1) | Tint |
| `glowColor` | HDR colour | (2, 1.3, 0.6, 1) | Glow colour (HDR) (with `GLOW`) |
| `glowScale` | range 0 to 4 | 1 | Glow alpha scale (with `GLOW`) |
| `glowPower` | range 0.1 to 8 | 3 | Glow falloff power (with `GLOW`) |
| `erosionSoftness` | range 0.01 to 0.5 | 0.08 | Erosion edge softness (with `EROSION`) |
| `erosionTiling` | float | 1 | Erosion noise tiling (per particle) (with `EROSION`) |
| `softness` | float | 0.5 | Softness (world units) (with `SOFT`) |
| `nearFadeStart` | float | 0.3 | Near fade: invisible at (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |
| `nearFadeEnd` | float | 1.5 | Near fade: whole from (world units from the camera) (with `NEAR_FADE`) |
| `distortionStrength` | range 0 to 0.2 | 0.03 | Distortion (screen UV) (with `DISTORTION`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_erosionTexture` | gray | Erosion noise (red channel) (with `EROSION`) |
| `u_distortionTexture` | gray | Distortion map (red: x, green: y; 0.5 shifts nothing) (with `DISTORTION`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GLOW` | off | Glow (alpha as light) |
| `EROSION` | off | Erosion (the particle's alpha dissolves it through a noise texture) |
| `SOFT` | off | Soft particles (fade where they meet geometry; reads the scene depth) |
| `NEAR_FADE` | off | Camera near fade |
| `DISTORTION` | off | Distortion (bends the scene behind the particle through a distortion map; reads the scene colour) |

## Post-processing

<a id="libraryblur"></a>
### Blur (`library:blur`)

A soft blur in one pass: 13 taps on two rings, averaged in linear light. For a wide or full-screen blur the engine's post-processing Blur (a quarter-resolution chain) is much cheaper; this one is for a chain of your own (with a pass scale below 1 it widens for free).

- **Type**: post-process (a pass of the scene's post-process chain); category Post-processing.
- **Inputs**: the previous pass's colour (`u_sceneColorTexture`) (the engine also binds `u_originalSceneTexture`, `u_depthTexture`, `u_gbufferTexture`, `u_ssaoTexture` to a pass declaring them).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | range 0 to 16 | 3 | Radius (source pixels) |
| `amount` | range 0 to 1 | 1 | Amount (0: the source as it is) |

<a id="librarycrt"></a>
### CRT (`library:crt`)

An old tube screen: barrel curvature, scanlines, an aperture grille, colour fringing and dark corners. A user post-process pass (the engine's post-processing has a cheaper CRT in its uber pass).

- **Type**: post-process (a pass of the scene's post-process chain); category Post-processing.
- **Inputs**: the previous pass's colour (`u_sceneColorTexture`) (the engine also binds `u_originalSceneTexture`, `u_depthTexture`, `u_gbufferTexture`, `u_ssaoTexture` to a pass declaring them).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curvature` | range 0 to 1 | 0.3 | Curvature |
| `lines` | float | 240 | Scanlines over the height |
| `scanlines` | range 0 to 1 | 0.5 | Scanline darkness |
| `mask` | range 0 to 1 | 0.3 | Aperture grille |
| `fringe` | range 0 to 4 | 1 | Colour fringing (pixels) |
| `vignette` | range 0 to 1 | 0.4 | Dark corners |

<a id="libraryedge_neon"></a>
### Edge Neon (`library:edge_neon`)

Glowing outlines: the picture's edges (Sobel on brightness) lit in a neon colour that can cycle through the hues, over a darkened scene.

- **Type**: post-process (a pass of the scene's post-process chain); category Post-processing.
- **Inputs**: the previous pass's colour (`u_sceneColorTexture`) (the engine also binds `u_originalSceneTexture`, `u_depthTexture`, `u_gbufferTexture`, `u_ssaoTexture` to a pass declaring them).

| `intensity` | range 0 to 4 | 1.5 | Edge brightness |

A four-shade handheld screen: big pixels, the brightness mapped to four greens with an ordered dither between them; for an exact palette use Post-processing ▸ Palette Quantize.

Big square pixels: the picture in blocks of a few output pixels, each the colour at its centre. Pair it with a pass scale below 1 to make it cheaper still.

<a id="libraryposterize"></a>
### Posterize (`library:posterize`)

Fewer colours: each channel rounded to a few levels, with an optional ordered dither that trades the bands for a fine pattern; for an exact palette use Post-processing ▸ Palette Quantize.

- **Type**: post-process (a pass of the scene's post-process chain); category Post-processing.
- **Inputs**: the previous pass's colour (`u_sceneColorTexture`) (the engine also binds `u_originalSceneTexture`, `u_depthTexture`, `u_gbufferTexture`, `u_ssaoTexture` to a pass declaring them).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |

| `saturation` | range 0 to 2 | 1 | Saturation |

<a id="libraryunderwater"></a>
### Underwater (`library:underwater`)

The view from inside a water: the scene fades into the water with the distance the view travels through it, each colour at its own rate (Beer-Lambert: a blue-green water loses red first), towards the water's colour lit by the sun and the ambient; the view leaving the water at its surface fades only by the water in front of it. Add it to the chain switched off: while the main camera is under a library:water surface (a running scene) the engine switches it on and gives it that surface's height and, with Follow water, its shallow and deep colours, and switches it off again above (Water, engine/core/object/environment/Water.h). Reads the scene depth: a depth pre-pass of the opaque meshes while it is on (none extra with SSAO or SSR); one full-screen pass.

- **Type**: post-process (a pass of the scene's post-process chain); category Post-processing.
- **Inputs**: the previous pass's colour (`u_sceneColorTexture`) (the engine also binds `u_originalSceneTexture`, `u_depthTexture`, `u_gbufferTexture`, `u_ssaoTexture` to a pass declaring them).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shallowColor` | colour | (0.25, 0.8, 0.85, 1) | Clear colour (the hue the view fades through) |
| `deepColor` | colour | (0.03, 0.25, 0.45, 1) | Water colour (what the distance fades to) |
| `visibility` | float | 6 | Visibility (world units: the clearest colour keeps 37%) |
| `waterLevel` | float | 0 | Surface height (world Y; the engine sets it under a water) |
| `followWater` | toggle | on | Follow water (colours from the water the camera is in) |

## Outline and stencil

<a id="libraryoutline"></a>
### Outline (`library:outline`)

Inverted-hull outline: the mesh pushed out along its smoothed normal (closed at hard edges) and drawn with its front faces culled, in one colour. Use it as an opaque material's extra pass, order After (Outline (hull) preset): the object's depth hides the inner hull. Not for blended objects: the hull's back faces fill the whole shape, which a blended object (no depth write) shows through Before and is covered by After; the Outline (hull) preset gives a blended material Outline (stencil), Visible only, instead. Width in pixels (constant at any distance, perspective or orthographic) or in world units (optionally growing with distance, capped). On hard-edged meshes the band beside a sharp corner is thinner than the width (down to width/sqrt2 in pixels, width/sqrt3 in world units, on a box): the hull follows the corner's smoothed normal so it stays closed. Works with skinning, morph targets and instancing; for Sprites use the Sprite shader's Outline feature instead (a flat quad has no hull). No shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Outline and stencil.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `smoothnormals`; `uv1` with `TEXTURE`; `rawcolor` with `VERTEX_COLOR_WIDTH`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, cull front, depth write on, shadows off.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outlineColor` | HDR colour | (0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 1) | Colour |
| `screenWidth` | range 0 to 32 | 3 | Width (pixels) (with `WIDTH_MODE_SCREEN`) |
| `worldWidth` | float | 0.03 | Width (world units) (with `WIDTH_MODE_WORLD`) |
| `distanceScale` | range 0 to 1 | 1 | Distance scaling (1: constant on-screen size beyond the reference distance) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `referenceDistance` | float | 10 | Reference distance (world width applies up to it) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `maxWidth` | float | 0.25 | Maximum width (world units) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `textureTiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Texture tiling (xy) and offset (zw) (with `TEXTURE`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_outlineTexture` | white | Tint texture (with `TEXTURE`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DISTANCE_SCALE` | off | Grow with distance (world width) |
| `TEXTURE` | off | Tint texture |
| `VERTEX_COLOR_WIDTH` | off | Width times vertex colour red |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WIDTH_MODE` | `WIDTH_MODE_SCREEN`, `WIDTH_MODE_WORLD` | Width in |

<a id="libraryoutline_stencil"></a>
### Outline (stencil) (`library:outline_stencil`)

QuickOutline-style outline that never covers its object: an extra pass After a main material that writes stencil 1 over its whole silhouette (Outline (stencil) preset: stencil always, ref 1, write mask 1, pass and depth-fail replace). Draws the pushed-out mesh where stencil bit 1 is not set. Visibility Always draws it through walls (give the object a sort priority above its occluders, as the preset does, so they draw first); Visible only depth-tests it: the outline of blended objects, which an inverted hull would fill (the Outline (hull) preset on a blended material, whose stencil also writes bit 1 over its draw-once or mask test). Width in pixels or world units, as Outline (thinner beside the sharp corners of hard-edged meshes, as Outline). Uses stencil bit 0x01. No shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Outline and stencil.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `smoothnormals`; `uv1` with `TEXTURE`; `rawcolor` with `VERTEX_COLOR_WIDTH`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, cull off (both faces), depth write off, depth test always, shadows off, stencil notequal ref 1 read mask 0x01 write mask 0x00; with `VISIBILITY_VISIBLE_ONLY`: depth write on, depth test less-equal.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outlineColor` | HDR colour | (1, 0.6, 0.1, 1) | Colour |
| `screenWidth` | range 0 to 32 | 4 | Width (pixels) (with `WIDTH_MODE_SCREEN`) |
| `worldWidth` | float | 0.04 | Width (world units) (with `WIDTH_MODE_WORLD`) |
| `distanceScale` | range 0 to 1 | 1 | Distance scaling (1: constant on-screen size beyond the reference distance) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `referenceDistance` | float | 10 | Reference distance (world width applies up to it) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `maxWidth` | float | 0.25 | Maximum width (world units) (with `DISTANCE_SCALE`) |
| `textureTiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Texture tiling (xy) and offset (zw) (with `TEXTURE`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_outlineTexture` | white | Tint texture (with `TEXTURE`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `DISTANCE_SCALE` | off | Grow with distance (world width) |
| `TEXTURE` | off | Tint texture |
| `VERTEX_COLOR_WIDTH` | off | Width times vertex colour red |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WIDTH_MODE` | `WIDTH_MODE_SCREEN`, `WIDTH_MODE_WORLD` | Width in |
| `VISIBILITY` | `VISIBILITY_ALWAYS`, `VISIBILITY_VISIBLE_ONLY` | Visibility |

<a id="librarysilhouette"></a>
### Silhouette (`library:silhouette`)

See-through silhouette: draws only the parts of the object hidden behind other objects (depth test greater, no depth write), in a flat colour or a fresnel glow, alpha blended. Use it as a material's extra pass, order Before (See-through silhouette preset), and draw the object after its occluders (the preset gives it sort priority 1). Each pixel blends once: stencil bit 0x02 is set where it draws (overlapping hidden parts do not stack). With the camera depth pre-pass on, the object's own depth is already in the buffer, so its self-hidden parts (the far side of a concave object) show too. No shadows.

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Outline and stencil.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `position`, `normals` with `SILHOUETTE_MODE_FRESNEL`.
- **Default state**: blend alpha, cull back, depth write off, depth test greater, shadows off, stencil notequal ref 2 read mask 0x02 write mask 0x02 pass replace.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | HDR colour | (0.25, 0.6, 1, 0.6) | Colour (alpha: opacity) |
| `fresnelPower` | range 0.25 to 8 | 2 | Fresnel power (with `SILHOUETTE_MODE_FRESNEL`) |
| `fresnelFill` | range 0 to 1 | 0.15 | Fresnel fill (opacity facing the view) (with `SILHOUETTE_MODE_FRESNEL`) |

| Keyword group | Values (first is the default) | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SILHOUETTE_MODE` | `SILHOUETTE_MODE_FLAT`, `SILHOUETTE_MODE_FRESNEL` | Shading |

<a id="librarystencil_mask"></a>
### Stencil mask (`library:stencil_mask`)

Writes stencil 16 (bits 0xF0) where it draws, and no colour or depth: a portal, window or hole. Objects with a stencil test show only inside it (Visible inside mask preset: equal 16) or only outside it (Visible outside mask: not equal 16). Masks must draw before their readers: in the opaque queue they precede blended readers; give opaque readers a higher sort priority or the mask a lower one (the Stencil mask preset sets -1). Several masks: refs 16, 32 ... 240 under read/write mask 0xF0. Alpha clip cuts the mask's shape from a texture's alpha. Turn colour writes on to see it (Colour).

- **Type**: mesh (a material's shader); category Outline and stencil.
- **Lighting**: none.
- **Inputs**: `uv1` with `ALPHA_CLIP`.
- **Default state**: blend opaque, depth write off, shadows off, colour write none, stencil always ref 16 write mask 0xf0 pass replace.
- **Depth program**: no (the built-in one).

| Property | Kind | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | (1, 0, 1, 1) | Colour (drawn only with colour writes on) |
| `alphaCutoff` | range 0 to 1 | 0.5 | Alpha cutoff (with `ALPHA_CLIP`) |
| `tiling` | vector4 | (1, 1, 0, 0) | Tiling (xy) and offset (zw) (with `ALPHA_CLIP`) |

| Texture | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `u_maskTexture` | white | Mask shape (alpha) (with `ALPHA_CLIP`) |

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ALPHA_CLIP` | off | Alpha clip shape |
